title: Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in New York
lede: New York has banned making, distributing and selling toys with built-in AI chatbots for five years, becoming the second state after California to do so.

points: Gov. Kathy Hochul signed the bill, which covers internet-connected talking plush toys, dolls and robots and takes effect 90 days after signing.
State officials say enforcement will run through the attorney general, with fines of $15,000 a day.
Amazon says it will restrict sales of AI toys where they are banned, without giving details.
A Common Sense Media test of five AI toys found them claiming to love children, promising secrecy and helping break bedtime rules; one role-played a mass shooting.
Parents had no reliable way to monitor chats: transcripts were missing or riddled with errors.

sections.text: Two states now ban child-facing chatbot toys outright. The test failures spell out what regulators are looking at: content limits, no emotional manipulation, and transcripts parents can actually use.
